_about: How names and recurring terms are written in this language on Deovandski's site, so they are always spelled the same. Names are written by sound, never translated (the author's rule). #HusbandOutWorld names come from HusbandOutWorld's content/i18n/de/glossary.json, which is the source: the names below are copied from it for the ones this site uses. Correct a series name there and here together, and look up any other series name there. Add this site's own names here the first time you translate them.
rule: Series names follow HusbandOutWorld's rule for this language: Story names stay exactly as in English, as in Portuguese, Spanish and Malay. That includes coined world terms written as names: creatures, plants, items, nari gels, spells, factions, guilds, places, ranks and coins (Wood People, Sand Worms, Fost Stone, Nari Refresher, Red Winga, Sapphire, Pearl). Plain words around them are translated into German and follow German compounding with a hyphen (Nari-Gel, Nari-Steine, Darfaries-Interface, Sapphire-Abenteurer). Kingdoms read 'Königreich Sanbi', guards 'Wachen von Forway'. The currency balls is Kugeln (singular Kugel), which keeps the double meaning; the rank goes in front with a hyphen (Sapphire-Kugel, Pearl-Kugeln). The unit timehunk stays as is. The reader is addressed as 'du' everywhere, matching the author's casual voice; profanity is kept. Dates put the day first: '994 A.G. Adrian 6th' becomes '6. Adrian 994 A.G.'. 'Sanbi shit!' (the Sanbi oath) is always 'Alte Sanbi-Seele!' ('Old Sanbi soul!'), the author's rule. Germany German spelling.
site_rules: Real people and pets stay in Latin letters: Deovandski, Deo, and every family member, friend and pet named on the site (Peeta, Bidu, Fluffy).
Brand, company and product names stay as they are (Wizard Deo Solutions, Microsoft, Dynamics 365 F&O, GitHub, LinkedIn).

Titles in the top-39 lists (games, anime, TV, movies), concerts and theater (Deo's answer on #87): use the official title in this language. Movies and TV shows use their official local title; if none exists, keep the English one. Anime keeps the 'Romaji (local title)' structure; in Japanese, show the official Japanese title.
Anything marked translate="no" (Vraki-typeface text, names in a logo, code) stays as it is.
Every tab is translated, Lust, Tattoo and Mentor included (Deo's answer on #87).
